newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori promotes troops who saved hostages.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori promotes troops who saved hostages.

text.p: The 140 elite commandos who took part in the rescue of 71 hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima will all be promoted a rank, President Alberto Fujimori said on Wednesday.
He also announced that the two soldiers who died in the rescue operation last week "will be declared national heroes."
Fujimori said he had already signed a decree for officials with positions below colonel to receive a promotion.

In order to promote colonels and above, a special law had to be passed, and this has already been sent to Congress, the president explained, while inaugurating two medical centres in Peru's southwest jungle region.

Fujimori also confirmed that armed forces had used a replica of the Japanese embassy building to practice the April 22 assault. "In truth, there's a duplicate of the Japanese residence, which also has tunnels. Rehearsals were carried out in detail and explosions were practiced," he said, without giving away the location of the mock-up.

Fujimori's troops rescued alive all but one of 72 hostages which Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels had held hostage for 126 days. Two soldiers and all 14 MRTA rebels died in the spectacular assault.
